_doc: AUTHORED. Modern locator control for the SOUTHERN CAMERAS of T-0467, and nothing else. These three junctions are not 1835 streets and are not georeferencing GCPs: they are the present-day crossings whose names the ticket used to say where it wanted a viewpoint — Sixteenth, Eighteenth and Cermak at Prairie Avenue — resolved to coordinates so that the anchors in data/scenes/1835.json stand where the ticket meant rather than where a round number fell. A CAMERA IS NOT A PLACEMENT. Nothing here claims a street, a lot or a building existed on 1835-07-01, and nothing in the structure layer may be offset from these points.
read_by: data/scenes/1835.json § anchors (note); tools/measure_anchors.mjs measures where they land
method: The rule is data/traces/street_control.json § node_rule, unchanged: the nodes SHARED by the two named surface roadways at the crossing, averaged, reprojected to EPSG:26916, and carried into the local frame by subtracting the datum origin (data/datum.json origin_utm_e 447072.7, origin_utm_n 4637395.8). Cycleways, footways and service ways are excluded, which matters here: East 18th Street has eleven cycleway segments mapped beside it under the name '18th Street Access Path', and averaging them in would pull the junction centre off the roadway.
how_good_these_are: Better than the control the box's own south wall was derived from, and it does not matter much either way. Two of the three are single-node crossings with no spread at all; Cermak & Prairie is two nodes of a divided roadway 16.13 m apart and is carried as their mean. What they inherit whole is the ±20 m the datum carries onto any 1834 reading (data/datum.json § derivation residual_note) — and these points are not being read against an 1834 sheet at all, so the honest statement is that each is the 2026 junction centre to within a metre or two, and that where it falls in the 1835 model is only as good as the datum. For a camera that is enough; for a placement it would not be, which is why this file is read by no generator.

cross_check.what: Cermak & Prairie against the box's own south wall.
cross_check.reading: This file puts Cermak Road at local N -3764.87. data/terrain/epochs/e1834_harbor_cut/terrain_spec.json § n_min derives Twenty-Second Street from the PLSS — one statute mile south of the committed State & Roosevelt section corner — at local N -3758.74, and notes that carrying the OSM square's own measured spacing instead puts it at N -3773.5.
cross_check.verdict: The junction falls 6.13 m south of the PLSS derivation and 8.6 m north of the measured-spacing one, i.e. between the two figures the terrain spec itself gives, and 35.13 m inside the box floor at N -3800. Two independent routes to the same street line agreeing to single-figure metres is a check on both; neither number is moved by it.

cermak_prairie.note: Cermak Road is divided here; the two nodes are the crossings of its two carriageways and the point is their mean, per the node rule.

not_control_for: the 1812 battle location, which T-0470 owns and which no anchor here claims
